title: Belle Gunness: The Black Widow of La Porte, Indiana (Full Documentary)
description: In April 1908, a farmhouse burned outside La Porte, Indiana. In the cellar were three children and a woman whose head was missing. Then the digging began.

This is the true story of Belle Gunness: a Norwegian immigrant, a widow twice over, and the woman at the center of one of America's most notorious murder cases. Men answered her newspaper ads and came to her farm on McClung Road. Many were never seen again. More than a century later, La Porte still doesn't know whether she died in that fire.

A La Porte Weather Now documentary. Narrated by a computer voice. Every photo, postcard and newspaper page is a real one, nearly all from 1908 or before (the cemetery and the university are shown as they look today). Maps and title cards were drawn for the film.

SEE IT IN PERSON

The La Porte County Historical Society Museum has a Belle Gunness exhibit: 2405 Indiana Ave., La Porte. Open Tuesday to Saturday, 10 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. (adults $5, under 18 free). Its program "Belle Gunness: The Mystery Continues" is Saturday, Nov. 7, 2026 (10 a.m.-noon and 1:30-3:30 p.m.; $5, tickets required): https://laportecountyhistory.org/
If you go looking for the old farm site on McClung Road, please respect private property.
